name: script
description: What a script reaches for, on demand: a recursive walk, a copy, a glob — each a method on text that loads the library on use.

api.sig: pub fn walk(self: text, suffix: text = "") -> vector<text>
api.doc:
Every file under the directory `self`, in every subdirectory, as paths joined with `/`
below `self`, in path order.  A symbolic link is never followed, so a loop in the tree is
not a loop here.  `suffix` keeps only the names that end with it (`".loft"`); `""` keeps
every file.  A path that is not a directory answers no files.

api.sig: pub fn copy_to(self: text, dst: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Copy the file at `self` to `dst`, bytes as they are: true when `dst` now holds them.  A
source that cannot be read writes nothing and answers false, as does a write that fails.

The paths that match the pattern `self`, in name order: `*` stands for any run of
characters inside one name, `?` for one character, and everything before the last `/` is
a directory taken as written (`"default/*.loft"`, `"out/??.txt"`).  A pattern without a
`/` is matched against the current directory.  An absent directory answers no paths.

api.sig: pub fn glob_match(pattern: text, name: text) -> boolean
api.doc:
Does `name` match `pattern`, with `*` any run and `?` one character?  A plain character
matches itself only.
